```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
library(ggplot2)
```

`MFO(ci = )` gives confidence intervals for the fit of one test (SPEC 13.1).
This article reports how often those intervals contain the true value in
simulated tests whose truth is known. The results were computed once, with
`inst/validation/bootstrap_coverage.R`, and are written into this article;
running the study takes about an hour, so it is not run when the article is
built.

## Design

Each simulated test comes from `simulate_MFO_sessions()`: one participant
from the default population (sedentary adults, Amaro-Gahete et al. 2018),
VO2max 3000 ± 400 mL/min, fat oxidation following a SIN curve (Chenevière et
al. 2009) and an error on the fat oxidation of each step with standard
deviation equal to a proportion of MFO (the noise CV, SPEC 17). The grid
crosses the method (P3, P2, MRER), the number of steps (6, 8, 10) and the
noise CV (5, 10, 20 %), with 200 tests per cell and B = 400 replicates per
interval. The truth is the Fatmax and MFO of the generating SIN curve.

Two caveats:

- **The truth is a SIN curve.** This favours the models closest to a SIN:
  P3 more than P2, and both much more than MRER. A different truth would
  give different biases.
- **Different draws.** The rows of the residual bootstrap and of the
  parametric interval come from two runs of the same design with different
  simulated tests; MRER was run with the residual bootstrap only.

## The ideal case

Before the grid, a test where the model is right: P2 fitted to a parabola
with 8 steps and independent normal errors (500 tests, B = 500).

| Interval | Coverage of Fatmax | Coverage of MFO | Mean width of Fatmax |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"bootstrap"` (modified residuals) | 0.882 | 0.892 | 1.93 %VO2max |
| `"parametric"`, fixed sigma (first version) | 0.892 | 0.896 | 1.95 %VO2max |
| `"parametric"`, sigma drawn (current) | 0.944 | 0.954 | 2.54 %VO2max |

The residual bootstrap and a parametric bootstrap with a fixed sigma behave
like a z interval: with n - p = 5 degrees of freedom their coverage is close
to P(|t~5~| < 1.96) = 0.893. Drawing sigma^2 from its posterior,
Inv-chi^2(n - p, s^2), carries the uncertainty of sigma and restores the
nominal coverage (binomial standard error 0.010).

## Coverage of Fatmax

```{r fig-fatmax, fig.alt = "Coverage of the 95 % interval of Fatmax against the number of steps, by method and noise CV, for the residual bootstrap and the parametric interval; a dashed line marks 0.95."}
ggplot(cov, aes(steps, coverage_fatmax, colour = method, linetype = ci,
                shape = ci)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~noise) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(6, 8, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Steps", y = "Coverage of Fatmax (95 % interval)",
       colour = "Method", linetype = "Interval", shape = "Interval") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

With the parametric interval, P3 covered 0.88-0.96 and P2 0.90-0.99 of the
true Fatmax; the residual bootstrap stayed at 0.75-0.94. P2 covers well at
high noise only because its intervals become very wide (next table). MRER
covered 0.48-0.74.

## Bias and width

```{r table}
tab <- cov[order(cov$method, cov$ci, cov$fat_noise_cv, cov$steps),
           c("method", "ci", "steps", "fat_noise_cv", "tests", "coverage_fatmax",
             "coverage_mfo", "width_fatmax", "bias_fatmax", "bias_mfo_pct")]
tab$fat_noise_cv <- 100 * tab$fat_noise_cv
names(tab) <- c("Method", "Interval", "Steps", "Noise CV %", "Tests",
                "Cover Fatmax", "Cover MFO", "Width Fatmax", "Bias Fatmax",
                "Bias MFO %")
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2)
```

Tests counts below 200 are tests in which the fit fell back to another
method (P3 to P2, MRER to MV), which gives no interval. The bias is the mean
estimate minus the truth (%VO2max for Fatmax, % of MFO for MFO).

```{r fig-bias, fig.alt = "Model bias of Fatmax (mean estimate minus truth, %VO2max) by method, number of steps and noise CV; MRER is about 3 to 4 %VO2max above the truth."}
ggplot(cov[cov$ci == "bootstrap", ], aes(steps, bias_fatmax, colour = method)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~noise) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(6, 8, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Steps", y = "Bias of Fatmax (%VO2max)", colour = "Method") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## What to use

- **`ci = "parametric"`** (or `ci = TRUE`) with **P3**: the closest to the
  nominal 95 %, with intervals that narrow as steps are added.
- **P2** is nearly unbiased at low noise, but at 10-20 % noise its vertex
  can fall far outside the measured intensities; `MFO()` warns and flags the
  interval then.
- **MRER** overestimates Fatmax by 3-4 %VO2max and MFO by 3-7 % against
  SIN curves, and its interval is centred on that bias. It is kept for
  comparability with published studies, not as the main method.
- With 6 steps every interval is less reliable; 8 or more are preferable.

## Reproducing

From the package source folder:

```
Rscript -e "devtools::load_all(); source('inst/validation/bootstrap_coverage.R')" \
  --args parametric cov_parametric.csv P3,P2
```

The script is resumable: each cell is saved when done and cells already in
the output file are skipped.
